entries.title: September 1, 2026
entries.markdown:
### Nav

- five entries and three panels, instead of eleven flat links (`0cd7351`)

### Agents

- the starters step aside once you start writing (`0e14ff5`)
- name the markdown storage instead of reaching through TipTap's Storage map (`11f4f51`)
- the real editor, and the formatting where Gmail puts it (`269d28b`)
- a reply counts everyone who will answer it, not just the To line (`e2e31f8`)
- tables are drawn, previews read as prose, and a duplicate bullet is swallowed (`2dabd0f`)
- a second "- " is a dash, not a nested list (`21422c6`)
- people are in the address book, and the connections wear their own colours (`4e4d73b`)
- the composer formats, and markdown is the only representation (`45f317a`)
- recipients are chips on To, Cc and Bcc — and every one of them runs (`8dc67ce`)
- the inbox rows say read or unread themselves, and Compose moves where mail keeps it (`4f46bbc`)
- Chrome was offering its own address book over the agent list (`8a35530`)
- reports get their headings, and a bold link label stops printing its asterisks (`ba3c703`)
- parenthesise the ?? beside the || (`44de900`)
- the inbox becomes mail properly — a task is a thread, and Sent is where it starts (`cd6e3e3`)
- how much a model may write in a round comes from how fast it writes (`3cec11f`)
- a round that runs out of room continues in the next one (`971f889`)
- deliver_report sends what the agent wrote, instead of making it write the report twice (`83a689f`)
- a running task pulses, because a reader must never wonder whether it died (`893adf0`)
- a search that found nothing says nothing, not "1 record" (`80e36c2`)
- the Researcher writes a section a round on Sonnet, because one long write is how you lose an hour's work (`01e52b7`)
- Amplify cuts a round off at 30 seconds, so the conversation is bounded rather than allowed to grow (`fbf98a6`)
- the inbox's open-a-task callback cannot be called onSelect (`0fa2ae8`)
- the Agentic Inbox — sidebar-09's mail block, repurposed by content (`9b95b50`)
- the round protocol and the way a run is drawn move out of the chat panel (`2717c5a`)
- the Researcher, and a round budget an agent sets for itself (`560dc66`)
- /agent goes to /agents (`0651f21`)
- a post's transcript line carries the message id, not just the word "posted" (`fa37d59`)
- PolicyBot's channel is a forum, so the first post learns to open a thread (`618e80f`)
- Discord, which is the test of whether the connection contract was real (`5d93321`)
- the Jurisdiction Guide was answering in emoji (`484ffa7`)
- don't-fill-the-gap moves from the Bill Reader into the ground all four stand on (`aff8d60`)
- "3 in" was a lie the cache told — the three input counts are disjoint (`d5c869c`)
- a round's prose is its own paragraph, and **bold** stops printing its asterisks (`4b81c76`)
- a bill number that came back different is a miss, not an answer (`3ecbb2d`)
- cache the prefix, because a run pays for every bill it has already read on every round after (`282eb21`)
- the Bill Reader stops elaborating a title into a paragraph (`73770ff`)
- the server counts the rounds the client drives, and brakes a stuck one (`54c0d2e`)
- the Slack app manifest, and one command that connects it (`0957c0f`)
- Amplify buffers the body, so the browser drives the loop a round at a time (`4730365`)
- the two agents that read one record read it on Sonnet 4.6, measured not assumed (`7250ed4`)
- the Money Follower can see the lobbying and FEC rows lane S just opened (`c4fdef5`)
- the chat route can frame the same events as SSE, because Amplify buffers ndjson (`ffb59ad`)
- a tool's input schema is JSON all the way down, and the vault's adoption trigger is written where the vault is (`51ab2e2`)
- four specialists on /agents, one tool loop, and the connection contract Slack is the first instance of (`1306e5f`)
- the buffered tool-call input is the SDK's DocumentType, not unknown (`e911359`)
- Bedrock answers through the site — Converse, streamed, on the models this account can actually invoke (`5527eb0`)

### Policy

- the assist panel finally has someone on the other end (`4cc22e8`)
- a member's vote history is bounded in SQL, not after the 1 MB cap (`f816953`)
- an unmatched bill number is a miss, never the newest bill (`6f7e7ac`)
- lobbying and FEC get a way in, gated to the jurisdiction that has them (`13d3d4f`)

### Search

- the chunk populator's summary line could not print its own result (`a19a6c8`)
- the chunk geometry lives in one place, because it drifted once already (`080dfa3`)
- the last 1.91 GB of bill text, and phrase search that tells the truth (`633928c`)
- a member is someone with a name, not a committee filed as one (`a765520`)
- a member search matches word by word, not as one string (`c697175`)
- cut the row set before ts_headline, not after (`7160206`)
- the verifier finds playwright wherever it already is (`c74ee64`)
- the menu goes national — each row wears its own jurisdiction (`3fe4c40`)
- cross-jurisdiction metadata is opt-in, because the menu still draws one flag (`e62bf2a`)
- /search shows a Text section, and every row wears its own flag (`81c2211`)
- every jurisdiction, and the bill text itself (`a592f66`)
- aliases, so 'holmes' finds Eleanor Holmes Norton (`75d8d0f`)
- /search wears the docs shell, and former members say so (`76757c0`)
- sitting members outrank former ones — SessionPeople holds only current rosters, so existence there is 'sitting now' in any jurisdiction (`b839639`)
- members from every jurisdiction, and a flag on every result (`e8b1052`)
- control the menu selection — it snaps to the top result when the query or its results change, instead of staying wherever cmdk left it (`efbddda`)
- Enter takes the first result — the see-all row's value follows the query so cmdk cannot keep it selected across searches (`4939875`)
- the header menu works, and /search shows everything it found (`4dfbb25`)

### Home

- one view over all 50 states and Congress (`1d0f6af`)
- drop the now-unused siteConfig import (`5a1738e`)
- the subheading is two lines — one view over all fifty states / Open Source. Open Code. Open Data. (`206bad7`)
- the hero says what govblock is — The Foundation for Civic Engagement; one view over all fifty states (`8fcc6c3`)
- Brendan's widget pass — Choose Session in the ⋮ menu, chamber pills, four widgets we never brought over, and an even bottom (`f57c5cb`)

### Fix

- two records are the same vote when they are the same roll call, not the same bill that day (`1d634ff`)
- house-votes was never registered, so the board's House cards never drew (`58cb10c`)
- CRS summaries are not text versions (`a2ff0a4`)
- a page that names one record reads in that record's jurisdiction (`9b78d44`)
- a subcommittee is not a "Subcommittee on Health Committee" (`b50f1b8`)
- follow member-votes and house-votes to the shapes lane C landed (`4f4bc4c`)
- a House card names the question it was asked, and votes on no bill still name themselves (`760226f`)
- the prerendered shell stops naming a jurisdiction nobody asked for (`760ba8e`)
- the four federal lists sort on the date they print (`b42cf08`)
- a committee page counted its own page of bills as the whole docket (`2306791`)
- the federal chamber reads "U.S. House", not "Congress House" (`7cea8d8`)
- a section falls back to its own committed rows, not to nothing (`82888bf`)
- the text timeline was printing the day it was fetched as the day the bill moved (`8826162`)
- bill= is honoured, and a scoped answer says what it was scoped to (`b43cece`)
- bill pages revalidate hourly instead of freezing at build time (`4f064a4`)
- a URL-borne scope becomes memory; the Chambers card takes the rail's compact size (`9df73bf`)
- the anti-flash script read localStorage.getItem(undefined) — the key crossed a client boundary (`c4db2ed`)
- the bills card's session picker listed Congress's sessions (`8c90f5f`)
- the Congress fixture may stand in only under Congress (`e6ff34f`)
- no Congress paint, scoped block previews, anchored rail calendar, no empty flag (`a079b7a`)
- scope the FEC explorer, and keep its keys off the network (`14fb5dc`)
- name the two national cards as national (`efa44bf`)
- the last four cards carry the scope in their links (`53debd2`)
- quote non-numeric array elements in the Data API shim (`052a25c`)
- reject non-integer bill ids before the Data API sees them (`769040d`)
- cast the text cap to int — the shim binds JS integers as bigint (`44fe9ac`)
- read the stream and bill texts within the Data API's 1 MB result cap (`3193641`)
- hand the Aurora identifiers to the SSR runtime, not just the build (`8ca0f89`)
- pass the Aurora resource identifiers into the Next server runtime (`6ddc8f6`)
- pagination without typeset bullets; Federal money → Finance (`0949ef4`)
- cap the stream at today; scope the changelogs to Congress + the jurisdiction (`542b9ac`)

### Chore

- drop the jurisdiction import the member page no longer reads (`e4f67c9`)

### Feat

- cosponsors, house votes with positions, CRS, the Record, communications (`e598d14`)
- the House floor on the Vote board, counted from the positions (`611d813`)
- nominations, reports, the Record and the laws — four docs the site never had (`992a0df`)
- a committee's own page, and the cards now go there (`e4439c3`)
- the member page — every name on the site now goes somewhere (`c5686af`)
- a bill's whole federal record on its own page (`0206e9f`)
- summaries, titles and related-bills, the last read both ways round (`5246c38`)
- serve the congress.gov families, in the API's own shape (`9a54ab3`)
- the newsroom and both changelogs follow the jurisdiction (`89cb3a2`)
- the home cards and the rails follow the jurisdiction (`e9f6521`)
- hearings follow the data; tallies named as New York's (`d325ae8`)
- the bills, committees and directory lists follow the jurisdiction (`78639f4`)
- the jurisdiction switcher chooses a jurisdiction (`75f41fb`)
- /api/policy/[resource] — every legislative read, scoped by jurisdiction (`3abd0ce`)
- every bill in the database has a page (`92d29d0`)
- /api/health — which database answered, and how fast (`c43dd28`)
- read the policy database through the Aurora Data API (`4f88b5b`)
- /typeset — the bill workspace, chat panel at the container's height (`f2b3621`)
- /create — the designer with one component, the card, in three versions (`aeaf4cf`)
- /calendar — month, week and day views, the hearings as events (`1bfefb7`)
- /blocks — the seven policy blocks, State/sidebar-07 dropped (landed in 0949ef4) (`d85da62`)
- changelog-v2 across every jurisdiction, bill text from the database (`dfab4f2`)
- /blocks — block viewer, tabs, /view iframe route, sidebar-07 (landed in 9fa7057) (`f5fea34`)
- stream and newsroom matviews on Neon; pages read them hourly (`b8c02ba`)
- calendar card with hearings by day; changelog across 51 jurisdictions (`6000dfc`)
- bill pages, changelog, changelog-v2, newsroom, directory; docs at 640px (`8d00c91`)
- home page and /docs bills + committees, ported from livingston-v3 (`92f45df`)

### Docs

- Chambers card in the bills rail, Party card in the directory rail (`bf0bbb0`)
- matview refresh is nightly on the box, not hourly (`9fa7057`)

### Perf

- newsroom — filter first, order second, never rejoin Bills (`c5a9db9`)

### Build

- hoisted node-linker so Amplify can package the runtime deps (`3c14c1b`)
- Amplify build spec for the pnpm monorepo (`1f73f92`)

- scope packages @govblock (`18e6b96`)

### Feat

- initial commit (`39df902`)
